I’m tracing the Drizzle schema wiring first so I can isolate why `generate` sees duplicates and why `up` cannot find a snapshot. Next I’m checking the schema entrypoints and migration layout, then I’ll patch the smallest root cause if it’s in the codebase.

The first local hypothesis is that Drizzle is loading both the schema barrel and the concrete schema files, which would explain every duplicate table/enum warning. I’m confirming that against the migration directories now, because the `up` failure may be a separate missing-snapshot problem rather than the same root cause.

I’ve confirmed the schema itself only defines each table once, so the duplicate warnings are almost certainly coming from how Drizzle loads the schema entrypoint. I’m checking the supported config shape next so I can patch the config in a way that matches this beta version instead of guessing.

The package search was noisy, but it confirmed the repo has the beta Drizzle CLI installed locally, so I can patch against the actual version in use. I’m narrowing to the config and migration metadata now; if the config accepts only a single entrypoint, that’s the cleanest fix for the duplicate-table problem.

The migration folder itself is empty, so the “outdated format” message is likely coming from Drizzle’s own migration state detection, not from checked-in files. I’m searching the workspace for any leftover `_journal.json` or older migration layout now; if there isn’t one, the config probably needs to be pointed at a single schema file rather than the directory barrel.

I have a concrete fix now: Drizzle’s own docs expect a single schema module, and this config currently points at the whole schema directory. I’m changing that to the barrel file so the CLI stops traversing the same table definitions twice, then I’ll rerun `generate` as the cheap falsifying check.
